scoring.strength_score: 0-100 composite detection-strength. Published per-term evidence used where available: detector scores (Your AI Slop Bores Me Hall of Shame), GPTZero AI Vocabulary frequency ratios, peer-reviewed ratios (Kobak, Juzek & Ward, Liang, Ward), and EQ-Bench / antislop slop-list rankings; otherwise banded by confidence tier (strong=75, moderate=50, context=30).
scoring.confidence: red=strong tell, orange=moderate tell, yellow=context-dependent (overuse only).
scoring.example: Optional illustrative sentence(s) showing the pattern. Populated for structural entries (sentence patterns, hook openers, rhetorical moves, formatting tells).
scoring.study_ratio: Peer-reviewed measured value, populated only where one exists. metric 'r'=frequency ratio (2024 vs expected); metric 'delta'=excess frequency gap (absolute prevalence increase).
scoring.note: Optional observed-frequency context (e.g. name dominance in controlled prompt tests).
scoring.names_caveat: Individual names are weak evidence alone (real people share them). They are tells in clusters, in AI-generation contexts, or for distinctive fantasy coinages. Only 'Elara' and a few full-name personas approach diagnostic on their own.

entries.term: Voice-emotion dialogue tag (voice laced/tinged/dripping with X)
entries.example: "You knew," she said, her voice laced with quiet fury.
entries.note: Six 'said voice [laced/tinged/dripping/filled/steady/trembling]' trigrams dominate the slop corpus; LLMs attach an emotion payload to nearly every tag.

entries.term: Emotion-cocktail construction ('a mixture of X and Y')
entries.example: Her eyes filled with a mixture of fear and awe.
entries.note: LLMs report two blended emotions instead of one; eyes-filled-mixture trigram cluster.

entries.example: Days turned into weeks, and weeks into months, as they rebuilt the village.

entries.term: 'A young woman named X' story opener
entries.example: In a small village nestled in the mountains lived a young woman named Elara.
entries.note: Canonical first line of unprompted LLM stories.

entries.term: Sunset scene-setting formula (sun hung low + casting shadows)
entries.example: The sun hung low in the sky, casting long shadows across the courtyard.
entries.note: sun-hung-low / low-sky-casting trigram chain; the assembled sentence is near-diagnostic.

entries.term: Chapter-end resolve formula ('ready to face whatever lay ahead')
entries.example: Together they turned toward the mountains, ready to face whatever challenges lay ahead.
entries.note: ready-face-whatever / challenges-lay-ahead trigram chain; LLMs close nearly every chapter on this beat.

entries.example: One thing was certain: nothing in Willow Creek would ever be the same.
entries.note: Portentous one-liner used to close scenes; slop trigram.

entries.term: 'The road ahead would not be easy'

entries.example: This claim is well documented.citeturn0search3 by multiple sources.
entries.note: Internal tool markup (ChatGPT/Grok/etc.) surviving copy-paste; unambiguous machine residue. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

entries.term: AI self-disclosure & cutoff-date hedge ("as of my last update", "I don't have access to real-time data")
entries.example: As of my last update, I don't have access to real-time pricing data.
entries.note: Broader companion to the existing 'As an AI language model' entry — covers training-cutoff and no-real-time-data disclaimer families. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

entries.term: Unfilled template placeholder ([Your Name], [INSERT X], TODO/TBD stub)
entries.example: Dear [Your Name], please review [INSERT SOURCE URL] before publishing.
entries.note: Slot-fill bracket never replaced before publishing. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

entries.term: Formulaic essay opener ("in the rapidly evolving landscape of X", "has emerged as a key X")
entries.example: In the rapidly evolving landscape of publishing, authors are adapting fast.
entries.note: Default LLM essay-opener template. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

entries.example: This could potentially create new opportunities for the whole team.
entries.note: Modal + hedge adverb stacked; either word alone is fine, the stack is the tell. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

entries.term: Social endorsement / CTA closer ("thank me later", "bookmark this", "don't sleep on this")
entries.example: Bookmark this: you'll want it later.
entries.note: Curatorial sign-off performing a recommendation without a reason to click. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

entries.term: Parenthetical hedging aside ("(and increasingly, X)", "(though to be fair, Z)")
entries.example: The plan worked (and increasingly, so did the backup plan).
entries.note: Pseudo-aside performing thoughtfulness without adding information. Detector ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license).

changelog.1.7: 2026-07-15: +7 entries + 10 structural-pattern regexes (lib/corpus/structural-patterns.ts) ported from github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing (MIT license) — chatbot citation markup leaks, AI-tool UTM params, cutoff/self-disclosure disclaimers, unfilled placeholders, formulaic essay openers, hedge-stacked predictions, social CTA closers, parenthetical hedging. Also fixed 3 pre-existing description-only entries (utm_source, Em-dash overuse, Title Case headers) that had no working matcher — same bug class as the participial-tail fix in 1.6, now given real regexes.
changelog.1.6: 2026-07-15: +9 entries — fiction dialogue-tag crutches (said gently/quietly, genuinely, I feel like, sympathy-check and therapy-speak dialogue lines) and anti-synthesis paragraph-closer clichés (unspoken understanding, said more than words, words left unsaid), sourced from a curated anti-AI-tell prose watchlist (PsycheFramework, Daystar79, GitHub). Companion structural pattern (abstract participial-tail clause) added to lib/corpus/structural-patterns.ts.
changelog.1.5: 2026-07-13: +184 entries from Wikipedia Signs of AI writing, GPTZero AI Vocabulary (3.3M docs), Kobak et al. 2025 (Science Advances), Juzek & Ward 2024/2026, Liang et al. 2024, Ward et al. 2025, Zhang et al. 2025 model fingerprints, and EQ-Bench/antislop fiction slop lists. New fiction wing (body language, emotional beats, atmosphere, structural tells, place names). -16 generic terms pruned as false-positive-prone (common human vocabulary with no measured AI skew).
